item.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria

item.title: INEC: 116,745 newly registered voters yet to collect PVCs in Lagos
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State says 116,745 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) of newly registered voters are yet to be collected. The Administrative Secretary of INEC in Lagos, Mrs Adenike Tadese, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday. Tadese said that the commission had received 177,295 PVCs belonging to eligible residents registered during Phase One of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in 2025. She said the commission’s weekly update as of Monday showed that 60,550 PVCs had been collected by their owners, leaving 116,745 cards awaiting collection. According to her, the uncollected cards represent a significant number of eligible voters who should collect their PVCs to exercise their franchise in the 2027 general elections. She said the cards were available for collection at the various local government offices of the commission across the state. “The cards are available for collection by their owners, not by proxy, at the various local government offices of the commission in Lagos,” she said. Tadese urged stakeholders to mobilise both old registrants who have not collected their cards and those who participated in the 2025 CVR exercise to collect their PVCs. She said the cards were still lying at INEC offices and appealed to their owners to collect them before the collection window closed ahead of the forthcoming elections. The INEC official also disclosed that PVCs belonging to eligible residents who registered during the 2026 CVR exercise before its closure would soon be ready for collection. Tadese, however, urged eligible registered voters to maintain orderliness during the collection of their PVCs. She reaffirmed the commission’s readiness to conduct free, fair and credible elections that would be acceptable to all stakeholders in the state. The administrative secretary also called for peaceful and orderly campaigns, urging all stakeholders to abide by the rules guiding the electoral process. She appealed to political actors and other stakeholders to play by the rules to ensure a peaceful electoral environment ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show
item.description: South Africa’s once-dominant African National Congress was headed for its worst-ever election performance Friday with about a third of support after 80 percent of the votes from local government polls had been counted. Wednesday’s municipal elections were dominated by concerns over failing water and power supplies in one of Africa’s wealthiest nations which became a democracy in 1994 when the ANC took power. With final results expected by Sunday, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC was still the largest party with 31.8 percent of votes after 80 percent had been counted. Projections released Thursday by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a state-funded research body, put its support at nearly 32 percent. This was its lowest score yet for the party after it secured just over 40 percent at the 2024 national polls and 46 percent at the previous municipal elections in 2021. At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. “This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared,” political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP. “It’s the ANC’s worst result in history.” “It will undermine its ability to exert authority across South Africa, not just at a local level, but frankly at a national level as well,” he told AFP. “And opposition parties will be smelling blood when it comes to the next election in 2029.” The party now led by President Cyril Ramaphosa has borne the brunt of criticism about years of municipal mismanagement that have left South Africans grappling with failing water supplies, persistent power cuts and crumbling public services. The pro-business, centre-right Democratic Alliance (DA) was placing second with 24.2 percent of votes, according to the 80 percent count. This was up from nearly 22 percent in the 2021 local government election. The post ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jude’s brother Jobe Bellingham gets England call-up
item.description: Jobe Bellingham was named alongside older brother Jude in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the first time on Friday as Chelsea’s Cole Palmer missed out. Fulham teenager Josh King is also handed his first call-up ahead of Nations League games against Croatia and Spain later this month. Tuchel said Palmer “misses too many opportunities” to impress at international level after pulling out of England’s last squad due to injury. The Chelsea star, who was not included for the World Cup, has been left out as Tuchel takes the chance to look at younger options with a place in the quarter-finals of the Nations League almost guaranteed Jobe Bellingham has been rewarded for a strong start to his second season at Borussia Dortmund, where Jude also played for three seasons before moving to Real Madrid. King has impressed despite Fulham’s struggles in the Premier League, while Liverpool’s 18-year-old winger Rio Ngumoha is also included. England are second in group A3 after four games, with three wins and a defeat, against Spain at Wembley. The Three Lions host Croatia, who they beat 7-0 last month, on Thursday before travelling to take on Spain with just one point needed to qualify for the knockout rounds in March. Newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is set to surpass Peter Shilton as England’s most capped male player after moving level with the former goalkeeper on 125 appearances against the Czech Republic last time out. Squad in full: Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton), James Trafford (Leeds) Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid/ESP), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle), Ezri Konsa, Ben White (both Arsenal), Djed Spence (Inter Milan/ITA), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen/GER) Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid/ESP), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund/GER), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze (all Arsenal) Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/GER), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona/ESP), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest) Vanguard News The post Jude’s brother Jobe Bellingham gets England call-up appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
item.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. item.title: King Charles’ Birthday: UK reaffirms commitment to stronger Nigeria ties
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr Pete Vowles, has reaffirmed the United Kingdom’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with Nigeria, describing the partnership between both countries as dynamic, reciprocal and ambitious. Vowles stated this on Thursday in Abuja at an event organised to celebrate the 78th birthday of His Majesty, King Charles III, and the longstanding relationship between the United Kingdom and Nigeria. Speaking on the theme of the celebration, GREAT, the High Commissioner said it reflected the strength of the relationship and the opportunities available for both countries to expand their cooperation. He said the partnership was exceptional in its content and continued to evolve in response to changing times, while maintaining mutual respect and equality. He said, “Well, we thought Great was a good way to talk about the great partnership that we have between the UK and Nigeria. A partnership that is exceptional in its content, but also I think it’s a partnership that is dynamic, it’s a partnership that is reciprocal, it’s a partnership that is ambitious.” Explaining the theme further, Vowles said, “And I say that because dynamic means it’s constantly evolving to the changing times. Reciprocal because it’s respectful, it’s two-way, it treats each other as equals. And ambitious because we know there is so much more we can do together.” The High Commissioner, expressed his determination to build on the progress recorded in relations between both countries, particularly following President Bola Tinubu’s state visit to the United Kingdom earlier in the year. Vowles said he would work to implement the agreements reached during the visit and explore further areas of cooperation for the mutual benefit of both countries. He urged Nigerians to contribute their ideas and energy towards strengthening the relationship, noting that there was room for greater engagement between the two countries. “We work hard together but we can do even more together. So bring your energy, bring your ideas and let’s do more together,” he said. Also speaking, the Country Director of the Royal Commonwealth Society, Nigeria Branch, Mr Blackson Olaseni Bayewumi, congratulated King Charles III on his 78th birthday and wished him many more years of service to the Commonwealth. Bayewumi, who described the King as an important link between the Royal Commonwealth Society and the Commonwealth, said His Majesty was the head of the Commonwealth and patron of the society. He said his relationship with the British High Commission in Abuja dated back to 1999, following Nigeria’s return to democratic rule and readmission into the Commonwealth after its suspension during military rule. According to him, the relationship had continued through various initiatives and programmes aimed at promoting Commonwealth values in Nigeria. He listed some of the activities as the Commonwealth essay competition, Commonwealth Spiritual Classics camp

item.title: Emergency delays: Doctors reject bill proposing 6-month jail term
item.description: The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has rejected proposed legislation seeking a six-month jail term or ₦300,000 fine for healthcare professionals over delays in emergency medical treatment. This is contained in a statement issued by the NARD President, Dr Ogar Idoko, in Calabar on Friday. Idoko described the proposed amendment to the National Health Act as punitive, arguing that doctors should not be criminalised for failures arising from inadequate healthcare infrastructure. He said the association recognised the importance of prompt emergency care and protecting patients but insisted that systemic challenges must be addressed before imposing criminal sanctions. According to him, doctors nationwide work under difficult conditions, including obsolete equipment, inadequate staffing, unreliable electricity and insufficient emergency medical supplies. “The challenges are consequences of longstanding institutional neglect rather than professional negligence, so I urge lawmakers to prioritise healthcare funding and infrastructure. “We also challenge the National Assembly to demonstrate similar legislative urgency in providing functional emergency departments, modern diagnostic equipment, reliable ambulance services and adequate personnel,” he said. He asserted that lawmakers should consider legislation compelling public office holders to use Nigerian government hospitals, with sanctions for misuse of public resources on avoidable overseas medical treatment. He warned that additional criminal penalties against overstretched healthcare professionals could worsen the country’s brain drain, popularly known as the “Japan syndrome.” He stated that the association acknowledged that the proposed bill reportedly contained safeguards for circumstances beyond practitioners’ control but insisted that such provisions must be explicit and enforceable. He called for the withdrawal and reconsideration of the proposed punitive provisions, alongside consultations involving healthcare associations, hospital administrators, patient representatives and other stakeholders. He urged the National Assembly to prioritise legislation guaranteeing adequate health funding, minimum emergency-care standards, appropriate staffing, constant electricity and functional referral systems. “We will consider all lawful options, including nationwide industrial action, if lawmakers proceeded with legislation unjustly criminalising doctors for institutional failures. “We however, pledged to make necessary arrangements to protect emergency and critically ill patients during any industrial action, while we reaffirm our commitment to patient safety and quality healthcare.,” he said. NAN reports that the Senate is considering a bill that seeks to punish hospitals and healthcare workers who refuse or delay emergency medical treatment. item.title: Troops arrest suspected terrorist in Plateau
item.description: …recover AK-47 magazine, ammunition By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have arrested a suspected terrorist, identified as Abubakar Ango, during a stop-and-search operation in Kukawa village, Wase Local Government Area of Plateau State. The suspect was reportedly arrested with an AK-47 magazine, 7.62mm ammunition, two mobile phones, suspected illicit drugs and the sum of N30,000 in cash. Military sources confirmed to newsmen in Jos that the arrest was made on Thursday during a routine security operation aimed at identifying and apprehending suspected criminal elements operating within the area. The sources disclosed that preliminary interrogation of the suspect reportedly linked him to a suspected terrorist syndicate allegedly led by one Kaura. They added that the suspect was currently in military custody undergoing further investigation to establish his level of involvement and identify other members of the alleged syndicate. The military sources urged residents to continue supporting the military and other security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist ongoing operations to rid the state of criminal elements. They stressed that public cooperation remained critical to the success of security operations and called on citizens to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements to the appropriate authorities. item.title: Africa Energy Bank: A Defining Test for Africa’s Energy Sovereignty and Just Transition
item.description: Why Africa’s newest financial institution must turn energy resources into energy access, industrial growth and lasting prosperity. By Ambassador Gabriel Aduda Chief Insight Officer, World Energy Council Nigeria Former Federal Permanent Secretary and Former OPEC Governor for Nigeria The formal establishment of the Africa Energy Bank (AEB) by the African Petroleum Producers’ Organisation (APPO) and the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), announced in Abuja on 31 October 2026, marks an important step towards African-led energy finance. The Bank has authorised capital of US$5 billion and is intended to finance projects across the energy value chain. Its establishment comes as traditional lenders reassess fossil fuel exposure, while African countries face urgent needs for electricity, clean cooking, infrastructure and industrial investment (APPO, 31 October 2026). The scale of the challenge is clear. The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates that about 600 million people in Africa lack electricity and more than one billion lack access to clean cooking (IEA, 2025). It also estimates that meeting Africa’s energy and climate goals will require annual investment exceeding US$200 billion by 2030 (IEA, 2024). The central question is whether the AEB can help meet these needs while strengthening energy security, affordability and sustainability. Its success will depend not only on the capital it mobilises, but on the quality of its governance, investments and development outcomes. Beyond Financing Extraction The AEB can help address financing constraints facing African energy projects. But its lasting relevance should not be measured only by how much oil and gas production it finances. A bank focused narrowly on extraction would risk repeating a long-standing pattern: exporting raw resources while importing refined products, equipment, technology and manufactured goods. Africa’s challenge is to convert energy resources into reliable power, competitive industries, jobs, local expertise and improved living standards. The AEB should therefore support integrated energy ecosystems, not isolated projects. A gas project, for example, should be assessed not only by production and export revenues, but also by its potential contribution to electricity, fertiliser, petrochemicals and industrial development. Renewable generation should be considered alongside the transmission, storage and distribution systems needed to deliver power reliably and affordably. Financing supply without the infrastructure and productive demand that make it useful will limit its impact. Financing the Energy Trilemma Africa must balance three related goals: energy security, energy equity and environmental sustainability. The priorities differ across countries and communities. item.title: US federal judge blocks Trump’s massive arch project
item.description: A US federal judge blocked President Donald Trump’s massive triumphal arch project on Thursday, casting doubt over the future of the project hours after it was green-lit by a public commission. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, who is overseeing the case, ruled that the Trump administration cannot start construction on the arch for two weeks while the court considers challenges to its legality. The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) had voted 8-4 to approve the project earlier Thursday, despite hearing hours of testimony from dozens of furious opponents who questioned its legality and purpose. Chief among the complaints was the location of the 250-foot (76-meter) tall structure: adjacent to the hallowed Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place for hundreds of thousands of American service members. The giant arch would be much taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, its inspiration. It would also tower over the Lincoln Memorial, directly across the Potomac River. The four dissenting commissioners had called for the decision to be delayed, noting there were legal concerns, a lack of congressional appropriation to fund the project and questions about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s claims of the arch’s military use. But the majority on the panel, which is controlled by Trump allies, voted against a delay and the Trump administration said it aimed to start work right away. Chutkan’s ruling sided with several veterans and the attorneys general of Washington and Virginia, who had sued seeking to halt construction of the arch. – ‘Illegal project’ – The arch is one of several projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the capital, many of which have prompted legal challenges. They include a White House ballroom, for which Trump had an entire wing of the presidential mansion demolished. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled that the plaintiff who filed suit to halt the project did not have standing. Another is the repeated renovation of the Reflecting Pool, a massive rectangular water basin on the National Mall. Trump has also proposed revamping the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic waterfront Washington golf course, cutting down hundreds of trees before a judge halted the project. The location, a traffic circle currently covered in grass, is key to the Trump administration’s defense of the project. Proponents claim that Congress approved the construction of a monument at the site over a century ago. However, that plan envisioned two large columns, meant to signify the North and the South in the US Civil War, not an arch. More than 100 people, often speaking as representatives of organizations, expressed their nearly unanimous opposition. item.title: Obono-Obla dismisses Atiku’s claim of insecurity in Calabar
item.description: Says Peter Obi incident isolated case A human rights activist and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress has dismissed recent claims of insecurity in Calabar by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as a product of gossip far from reality. Speaking on a national television station, Obono-Obla was emphatic that the Cross River State Capital has no security issue. According to him, “Calabar is one of the safest cities anybody would want to live in Nigeria,” and lauded Governor Bassey Otu for providing effective and efficient security measures in the state. In his words: “The governor has addressed security in Calabar. Before the governor came into office, I was very familiar with the security situation. University lecturers and doctors were being kidnapped almost every day. But as soon as he came into office, he appointed a retired Major General as state security adviser. “The governor has also provided significant security support, including government police officers and other security agencies.” While accusing Atiku of relying on gossip, he said “it is very petty for somebody who was a former Vice President of this country to descend to that level and begin talking about security in Calabar.” On the incident involving the campaign convoy of Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, the former presidential aide said stone-throwing during campaigns, even in advanced democracies like the United States. While describing the incident as an isolated case, he wondered if the incident was not as the result of internal disaffection within Obi’s own party. item.title: 14-year-old girl shot as gunmen attack farmers in Nasarawa
item.description: A 14-year-old girl, identified as Amina Ya’u, has sustained gunshot injuries after suspected armed herders opened fire on farmers in Majelisa village, a community bordering Nasarawa and Plateau states. The incident reportedly occurred at about 6:30am on November 5 following reports of sporadic gunshots in the community. Security sources disclosed the development to Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, saying troops of Sector 9, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), deployed at Jenta, immediately responded to a distress call and moved to the scene. According to the report, the troops found the teenage girl with gunshot wounds, while the suspected attackers had fled before their arrival. “Preliminary investigations indicated that a group of armed herders allegedly opened fire on farmers following a disagreement over grazing activities,” the report stated. The troops subsequently evacuated the injured girl to the General Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, for medical attention. Zagazola Makama said engagements with Fulani leaders were ongoing to assist security operatives in identifying and locating the fleeing suspects. It added that troops had intensified patrols and increased their security presence in the area to prevent further violence and possible escalation of the dispute. The incident adds to a series of attacks reported in Nigeria’s North-Central region in recent months. For decades, clashes involving herders and farming communities in the region have resulted in deaths, destruction of farmlands and loss of cattle, amid persistent disputes over land use and grazing activities. item.title: Trump bars future presidents from altering Oval Office
item.description: US President Donald Trump has signed an order designating the Oval Office as a national monument, a move he said would prevent future presidents from altering or demolishing the historic space. Trump signed the order on Thursday, extending his focus on White House renovations despite a major midterm election defeat suffered by his Republican Party. Critics have accused the president of paying more attention to construction and renovation projects in Washington than to voters’ concerns over the war in Iran and the rising cost of living, issues that featured prominently ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections. A day after Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump largely ignored the electoral outcome and instead showcased construction work on a new White House ballroom. On Thursday, his attention shifted to the Oval Office, which he has decorated with gold ornaments since returning to power last year, as well as the adjoining Cabinet Room. Trump said the proclamation was intended to protect the two rooms from future alterations. “It won’t be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched, or anything else. It’s called actually a national monument,” he told reporters. The president said the order would make it impossible for future occupants of the White House to carry out building work on the two rooms. The move, however, has fuelled speculation that Trump could be considering further changes to the West Wing, following earlier suggestions that he might relocate reporters from the White House briefing room, which is close to the Oval Office. Trump’s signing of the order was not broadcast by major US television networks. The White House has excluded CNN from the rotating pool of television outlets covering presidential events. The president, however, made a reference to the midterm elections, placing a red baseball cap bearing the word “veto” on the Resolute Desk in front of him. Trump, 80, has threatened to use his presidential powers to block Democratic-backed legislation, although he has also said he is willing to work with the opposition party. item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ set for blockbuster return after 13 years
item.description: Fans of the violent “Grand Theft Auto” video game franchise are just two weeks away from getting their hands on the latest edition, which has taken almost a decade to make and has become the most expensive title in history. The franchise allows players to act out gangster fantasies — shooting up bars, crashing cars — in fictional renderings of US cities where the soundtrack piped through in-game radio is almost as important as the cutting-edge visuals. GTA VI, which comes 13 years after its predecessor, is expected to break sales records when it lands on November 19 thanks in part to a monumental marketing campaign that kicked off in late 2023 with the first official trailer. “It is going to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time,” Chris Dring of The Game Business outlet told AFP. The previous edition, GTA V, is still the second-biggest selling game ever — it took just three days to rack up $1 billion in sales, two days less than the movie “Avengers: Endgame”. The budget of GTA VI has reportedly ballooned to over $1 billion — far higher than any other game or film — and projections have it on track to make several billion in its first week, which would smash all records for any cultural product. – ‘Top creators’ – ‘GTA VI’ has two main protagonists, former drug-runner Jason and newly released ex-con Lucia, who try to survive in Vice City, a reimagining of Miami. Lucia is the first playable woman character in a main edition of the almost 30-year history of a franchise. During the 1990s and 2000s the game’s graphic depictions of sex, violence and misogyny became notorious — tabloid media outrage boosting the title’s notoriety and helping sales to skyrocket. Rockstar Games has spent eight years developing the sixth edition, a process beset by difficulties including the leak of development footage and code for the game online in 2022. But expectations are sky-high. “They’ve spent a long time on this game, but they are probably the top game entertainment creators in the world,” said Dring. Analysts expect the game to have an impact on the entire video game sector, including on console sales and accessories. Several other studios delayed the release of new games to avoid being caught in the hype cycle around GTA VI. Analysis firm Sensor Tower said the game had already generated around $750 million from pre-sales. Surveys suggested almost one-third of the 49 million people who use PS5 and Xbox Series consoles in the United States intended to buy the game. “The purchase intent that we’re seeing on ‘Grand Theft Auto’ is far away above any other game we’ve ever tracked,” said Mat Piscatella of consultancy Circana. “For me, it’s the game of the decade,” Jocelin Lebeau, 39, a gamer who works for the French military, told AFP at a recent event in Paris. “I’m ready to buy it sight unseen.” The post ‘Grand Theft Auto’ set for blockbuster return after 13 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EPL: Carrick fights for Man Utd job ahead of international break
item.description: Michael Carrick takes charge of Manchester United for what could be the last time against Aston Villa this weekend as he battles to save his job despite a morale-boosting midweek victory over Roma. United’s dramatic win in the Champions League gave the coach breathing space but he remains under intense pressure ahead of the international break. Elsewhere in the Premier League, Manchester City will be seeking to avoid a rare third straight league defeat when they face Nottingham Forest as they try to keep pace with leaders Arsenal. AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of the action: Carrick’s last chance? When Manchester United’s players trudged off at half-time against Roma on Tuesday, 2-0 down and seemingly out of ideas, Michael Carrick’s fate appeared to be sealed. Instead, his underperforming team somehow turned things around, with Matheus Cunha scoring two late goals in a 3-2 win at a feverish Old Trafford. It ended a run of nine games without a victory — United’s longest winless run since the 1988/89 season. Defender Diogo Dalot said he hopes the Roma result can kickstart their season. “Nights like this can change momentum, can change seasons, and I think this win is going to give us confidence for the next games,” he said. But the brutal reality is that United could be bottom of the Premier League when they kick off on Sunday if results go against them. Whatever the outcome, the international break will give the club’s hierarchy an opportunity to consider their long-term options. Villa’s Spanish manager, Unai Emery, was tipped as a potential candidate for the Old Trafford hot seat but reports suggest he is close to signing a new deal with the Birmingham club. Two-way title race? Manchester City know that even if they keep pace with Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain. The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment. Arsenal appear to be the only other serious contender for the title, having the happy knack of winning even when below par. On paper, both clubs face a straightforward task this weekend, though City’s trip to Nottingham Forest could be trickier than it looks. Opta’s “expected points” table, which orders the Premier League based on expected goals for and against, has Oliver Glasner’s team in third — a remarkable 16 places higher than they are in the real table. Arsenal, who host struggling Hull, have won 18 of their past 19 Premier League games against promoted sides. Things looking up for Spurs The doom and gloom around Tottenham has lifted after a three-game winning streak in the Premier League under manager Roberto De Zerbi. Less than three weeks ago Spurs, without a single win, propped up the division. They are now comfortably placed in mid-table. item.title: Bullem takes over as C’River PDP Chairman
item.description: …as Party Backs Wike’s Rainbow Coalition By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Cross River State has ratified Chief Francis Bullem as its substantive State Chairman, while pledging loyalty to its national leader and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, and endorsing his Rainbow Coalition. The decisions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the party’s State Executive Committee, SEC, meeting held on Thursday at the party’s State Secretariat in Calabar. The communiqué, signed by the State Publicity Secretary, Mr Mike Ojisi, said the SEC acknowledged and accepted the resignation of the former State Chairman, Mr Venatius Ikem. It said the committee approved Bullem’s nomination and subsequently ratified him as substantive chairman in line with Article 47, Sections 5 and 6 of the PDP Constitution (2017), as amended. Vanguard gathered that the development is expected to usher in a new leadership phase for the party in the state. The SEC also endorsed the Rainbow Coalition led by Wike, a former Rivers State governor, describing him as the party’s national leader. The endorsement signals the state chapter’s support for the political platform he leads. The committee expressed concern over what it described as incessant attacks on PDP members and members of other opposition parties while carrying out legitimate political activities across the state. It condemned the attacks and reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the rights of party members to participate freely in lawful political activities. The communiqué stressed the need for an atmosphere in which political parties and their members could operate without intimidation or harassment. The SEC reiterated its commitment to the party’s constitutional provisions and political activities in Cross River. It would be recalled that Ikem resigned from the PDP on October 16, citing internal divisions, a crisis of direction and leadership incoherence within the party. item.title: 2027: INEC chairman seeks traditional rulers’ support for credible polls
item.description: ….Commissions BVAS storage centre in Kogi By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, has sought the support of traditional rulers in Kogi State for the conduct of peaceful, transparent and credible elections ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan made the appeal on Thursday in Lokoja during an engagement with traditional rulers from the 21 local government areas of the state. The INEC chairman said he visited the state alongside his team to assess the preparedness of the commission’s personnel and infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections and the forthcoming off-cycle governorship election. He said the commission was committed to strengthening its operational capacity through infrastructure upgrades and the deployment of modern technological tools to ensure seamless electoral processes. Amupitan urged traditional rulers to use their influence and close relationship with grassroots communities to promote peaceful conduct, voter awareness and acceptance of credible electoral outcomes. Speaking at the engagement, the Kogi State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Shehu Wahab, commended the traditional rulers for their sustained cooperation with the commission. Wahab said the support of traditional institutions remained vital to successful electoral activities, particularly in promoting peace and encouraging citizens to participate actively in the democratic process. Responding, the traditional rulers pledged to communicate the INEC chairman’s message to their subjects and assured the commission of their commitment to peaceful, transparent and credible elections in the state. Earlier, Amupitan commissioned the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) storage centre at the INEC state headquarters in Lokoja as part of efforts to strengthen the commission’s operational infrastructure ahead of future elections. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
item.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. item.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
item.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. Osunbor said the party would appeal the judgment to ensure that a higher court sets it aside. He expressed optimism that Atiku would survive the current challenge, insisting that the former Vice President had the support of the people. “Atiku will survive because the people are behind him. The force of the people will be greater than the force of those who want to enslave Nigerians,” he said. Osunbor’s comments followed Thursday’s judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated actions taken by the party under the leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the ADC. The party has rejected the ruling and vowed to challenge it at the appellate court.
